The series is strongly seasonal with unstable ranking; a simple mean may provide a robust baseline to compare against weighted.
test a different weight type (softmax_neg_error) to see if a smoother weighting beats inverse_error while still robust to unstable ranking.
try a per‑horizon weighted combination to exploit that different models win at different horizons, motivated by unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
test a robust DBA combination to see if it beats mean in this unstable, highly seasonal series.
test a mean combination on the reduced, low‑error pool (trend 0, strong seasonality, unstable ranking) to see if a smaller robust subset beats the full‑pool mean.
Test a weighted combination on the stable, top‑7 pool to see if focusing on the best performers improves over the mean, motivated by the unstable ranking hint.
Test a robust median combination on the full model pool to see if it beats the simple mean under unstable ranking.
Test a forward‑selection weighted combination on the full pool to see if a sparse subset improves robustness in this highly seasonal, unstable‑ranking series.
The series is strongly seasonal and ranking unstable; a per‑horizon weighted scheme on a smaller, more diverse pool (pool4) might capture complementary strengths without over‑fitting to noisy errors.
test robust median on correlated subset

decision.justification: Selected 'mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 1.0. Series context: trend strength 0.0 and seasonal strength 0.7499; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.037); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.429.
